title: Therapeutic mechanisms of psychedelics and entactogens | Request PDF
abstract:
Request PDF | Therapeutic mechanisms of psychedelics and entactogens | Recent clinical and preclinical evidence suggests that psychedelics and entactogens may produce both rapid and sustained therapeutic effects...
... Several studies have supported the notion that psychedelics like psilocybin may act as "psychoplastogens", with their acute effects initiating circuit plasticity and enduring brain and behavioural changes
[74] presented two interrelated hypotheses to explain the clinical improvements in psychiatric conditions observed with psychedelic treatments: the "psychoplastogenic" hypothesis, which emphasizes the neuroplastic effects of these substances, and the "behavioral catalyst" hypothesis, which suggests that the therapeutic benefits derive from consciousness-altering experiences and mystical encounters, especially when combined with psychotherapy.
Treatment guidelines Treatment recommendations of the SGPP for the treatment of mental illnesses with psychedelics
However, no consensus exists with regard to the therapeutic mechanisms of action, and clinical efficacy is explained by competing but not mutually exclusive models, differing in the relative contribution of psychoplastogenic versus behavioural catalytic effects of MDMA
